title: Seven cities of Delhi: from Lal Kot to Shahjahanabad
seo_title: Seven Cities of Delhi: History, Rulers and What to See
meta_description: The seven cities of Delhi explained: Lal Kot and Qila Rai Pithora, Siri, Tughlaqabad, Jahanpanah, Firozabad, Dinpanah and Shahjahanabad, and how to walk them.
keywords: seven cities of delhi in order
summary: The seven cities of Delhi are a traditional count of the walled capitals built in the Delhi area: Lal Kot and Qila Rai Pithora, Siri, Tughlaqabad, Jahanpanah, Firozabad, Dinpanah (Purana Qila) and Shahjahanabad. Historians count them differently, and some lists reach eight or more, but each left ruins you can still walk.

sections.h2: Why Delhi has seven cities (or more)
paras: Delhi sits between the Aravalli ridge and the Yamuna, a natural crossing on the route between the north-west and the Ganga plain. Rulers kept founding new walled settlements here rather than reusing old ones, partly for prestige, partly for defence and water, and partly because the population moved with the court.

The number seven is a convention, not a rule. Some historians count Lal Kot and Qila Rai Pithora as two cities; some leave out Jahanpanah, which was really a wall joining Qila Rai Pithora and Siri; some add Kilokhri of Kaiqubad, Mubarakabad of the Sayyids, Sher Shah's Delhi, or New Delhi as an eighth. Excavations at Purana Qila also show settlement going back to the Painted Grey Ware period, long before any of these cities. The list below is the one most often used on walks and in textbooks.

sections.h2: Lal Kot, Qila Rai Pithora and Siri
paras: Lal Kot is traditionally credited to the Tomara ruler Anangpal and dated to the 11th century. The Chauhans, under Prithviraj III (Rai Pithora), extended it into a larger fortified city. After 1192 the new Sultanate rulers built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and Qutb Minar inside it. Today [the Qutb complex](the-qutb-complex.html) and Mehrauli Archaeological Park are the best places to see the rampart lines and the buildings that grew within them.

Siri was built by Alauddin Khalji around 1303, at a time of repeated Mongol attacks. Little remains beyond sections of wall, but the Siri Fort landscape walk traces them. Alauddin's great tank, the Hauz-i-Alai, served Siri; it was later restored by Firoz Shah and is now the lake at [Hauz Khas](hauz-khas.html).

Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq built Tughlaqabad on a rocky outcrop in only a few years. Its sloping walls and bastions are the most dramatic fortifications in Delhi. His tomb, linked to the fort by a causeway across what was once a lake, is covered on the Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's Tomb focus walk, and the fort itself on the [Tughlaqabad Fort walk](tughlaqabad-fort.html).

His son Muhammad bin Tughlaq enclosed the populated area between Qila Rai Pithora and Siri with a wall, creating Jahanpanah (refuge of the world). Its surviving buildings include the palace platform at [Bijay Mandal](bijay-mandal-the-city-of-jahanpanah.html), the large Begumpur mosque and the Satpula waterworks, a dam with seven arches.

Firoz Shah Tughlaq moved north to the Yamuna bank and founded Firozabad in 1354. Its citadel, now [Firoz Shah Kotla](firoz-shah-kotla.html), still has the Ashokan pillar he brought from Topra mounted on a pyramidal palace building.

Humayun began Dinpanah (refuge of the faith) in 1533 on the old mound beside the Yamuna. Sher Shah Suri, who drove him out in 1540, rebuilt it; most of what stands at [Purana Qila](purana-qila.html), including the Qila-i-Kuhna mosque and the Sher Mandal, dates to Sher Shah's time or to Humayun's return.

Shah Jahan moved the Mughal capital from Agra to Delhi and built Shahjahanabad between 1639 and 1648. The [Red Fort complex](red-fort-complex.html), a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007, was its palace-fortress, and the city's Friday mosque is covered on the Jama Masjid and Shahjahanabad walk. Old Delhi's lanes still follow much of its original plan.

sections.h2: How to walk the seven cities of Delhi
paras: You cannot see all seven properly in one day, but you can see the sequence. A practical plan is to take the southern cities together (Qutb, Mehrauli, Tughlaqabad and Jahanpanah) on one morning, and the northern ones (Purana Qila, Firoz Shah Kotla and Shahjahanabad) on another. Our full-day [Delhi through seven cities](delhi-through-seven-cities.html) programme picks the strongest stop from each. For context, read our guides to the Delhi Sultanate and the heritage walk in Delhi. Check the ASI website for current entry rules before you go.

faq.q: What are the seven cities of Delhi in order?
faq.a: The usual list is Lal Kot and Qila Rai Pithora (Tomaras and Chauhans), Siri (Alauddin Khalji), Tughlaqabad (Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq), Jahanpanah (Muhammad bin Tughlaq), Firozabad (Firoz Shah Tughlaq), Dinpanah or Purana Qila (Humayun and Sher Shah Suri) and Shahjahanabad (Shah Jahan).

faq.q: Which is the oldest city of Delhi?
faq.a: Among the seven, Lal Kot, associated with the Tomara rulers in the 11th century, is the oldest. Archaeologically, Purana Qila has much older layers, with Painted Grey Ware from the 1st millennium BCE, and an Ashokan edict at Srinivaspuri shows Mauryan presence.

faq.q: Why do historians count the cities of Delhi differently?
faq.a: Because the boundaries are blurred. Lal Kot and Qila Rai Pithora are one city to some and two to others; Jahanpanah was a wall joining existing settlements; and short-lived towns like Kilokhri or Mubarakabad, and New Delhi, are sometimes added. Seven is a convention, not a fixed count.

faq.q: Is New Delhi the eighth city of Delhi?
faq.a: It is often called the eighth city. New Delhi was designed by Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker after the 1911 decision to move the capital from Calcutta, and was inaugurated in 1931. Its centre is Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath).

faq.q: Can I see all seven cities of Delhi in one day?
faq.a: You can see one strong site from each in a long day, but it involves a lot of driving. Most groups do the southern cities (Qutb, Mehrauli, Tughlaqabad, Jahanpanah) and the northern ones (Purana Qila, Kotla, Shahjahanabad) on separate mornings.

posts.hook: Delhi's seven cities might be six, eight or eleven.
posts.caption: It depends who is counting. Lal Kot and Qila Rai Pithora are sometimes one city; Jahanpanah was really a wall; New Delhi is often called the eighth.
Delhi's early capitals sit on the rocky ridge in the south. Each later one moves closer to the Yamuna, ending at Shahjahanabad. Plan your walks south to north.
